qt: to the Commission Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE) Subject:

On 23 September 2026, an 87-year-old tenant with a disability was evicted by an investment company from her home in Madrid after having lived there for 71 years. She had never missed a rent payment, and the UN Committee on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights had requested that the eviction be suspended. In 2025, Spain carried out more than 25 000 evictions. Principle 19 of the European Pillar of Social Rights guarantees vulnerable people protection from forced eviction, and the EU is a party to the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities. 1.

In the negotiations on the proposed Council Recommendation on fighting housing exclusion, will the Commission defend the standard that no vulnerable person may be evicted without adequate alternative housing?
Will it recognise security of tenure as an affordability tool in the European Semester, and ensure that country-specific recommendations support national measures that extend tenancies?
Will it add a harmonised eviction indicator to the Social Scoreboard?
at: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) The case referred to in the question touches on challenges affecting many people across Europe, including evictions, security of tenure, insufficient social and affordable housing and the effects of speculative investment on housing affordability and security. The Council Recommendation on fighting housing exclusion, including homelessness, adopted on 19 October 20261, takes a strong preventive approach to housing loss. It calls on Member States to strengthen prevention of and protection against forced evictions and to support people at risk of losing their homes, particularly those in vulnerable situations, through a range of measures. The Recommendation also addresses security of tenure and long-term stable housing solutions as key components of prevention policies. Housing affordability and access to social and affordable housing are monitored through the European Semester. The 2026 Country Report for Spain identifies significant affordability pressures, a limited stock of social housing and particularly acute challenges in high-demand areas. The Semester provides a framework for monitoring the social impact of housing developments and supporting policy responses to housing insecurity. The Recommendation also emphasises strengthening data collection and monitoring through indicators to assess the effectiveness of national policies, including preventive measures. The Commission will review progress, including in the context of the European Platform on Combatting Homelessness2, based on Member States reports and, where necessary, with the development of relevant statistics and indicators, along with appropriate monitoring frameworks.
